edges.description: The obstructed gland is the site where staphylococcal infection becomes established.
Staphylococcal growth inside the meibomian gland drives acute local inflammation.
Suppuration in the meibomian gland produces the internal stye centered within the tarsal plate.
The acute suppurative inflammation makes the lesion painful.
Local inflammation produces redness of the affected eyelid.
Abscess formation and inflammatory edema swell the eyelid.
An unresolved internal hordeolum can become chronic and develop into a chalazion.
Severe or unresolved infection can spread beyond the meibomian gland into adjacent eyelid tissue.
